parts.label: a
parts.ask: The graph of \(y = 3|x-2| + 5\) has its vertex at \(P\). Find the coordinates of \(P\).
parts.method: The vertex is where the inside of the modulus is zero

steps.why: \(|x-2|\) is never negative, so \(y\) is least when \(|x-2| = 0\).

parts.label: b
parts.method: Split the modulus into its two branches, then check each answer

steps.why: Each branch of the V is a straight line, valid on its own side of \(x = 2\).
\(\tfrac{17}{7} = 2.43\ldots\), which is \(\geq 2\): it is on this branch, so keep it.
But this branch needs \(x < 2\), and \(5\) is not less than \(2\): reject it.

parts.label: c
parts.ask: The line \(y = kx + 4\) meets \(y = 3|x-2| + 5\) at 2 distinct points. Find the range of values of \(k\).

steps.text: Every line \(y = kx + 4\) passes through \((0, 4)\), which is below the V. To meet the V twice, the line must pass above the vertex \(P(2, 5)\) and cross both branches.
steps.why: A sketch makes this clear: rotate a ruler about \((0, 4)\).
At \(k = \tfrac{1}{2}\) the line just touches the vertex: only one point. So \(k > \tfrac{1}{2}\).

steps.text: The right branch has gradient 3. At \(x = 2\) the line is already above the vertex, so if \(k \geq 3\) it climbs at least as fast as that branch and never meets it. So \(k < 3\).
steps.why: This upper limit is the one most people missed.
